prompt.context: Your client is a real estate developer, Lizette's Luxury Properties, and is currently assessing a new project idea in Costa Rica. Costa Rica has a beautiful coastline which has historically been difficult to access. The nearest airport was over six hours away. As of last year, a new airport was constructed only a half hour away. There has been an investment boom in the region due to the increasing number of tourists (popular with Americans and Asians). The Mandarin Oriental and The Four Seasons, two prominent luxury hotel chains, were the first to enter this market with a 250-room hotel each.
prompt.question: Should your client invest in the tourism opportunity created by the new airport? Would you recommend that s/he enter the market?

clarifying_info.q: What has the client done in the past?
clarifying_info.a: The client has focused on hi-rise apartments (50%) and luxury condominiums (50%) in the past but wants to enter the hotel arena. They have focused on world-class beaches such as Playa del Carmen, Marbella, Coral Beach, Tahiti, Fiji, Maldives, and Mikonos.

clarifying_info.q: How many tourists visit the region?
clarifying_info.a: 875,000 tourists per year (assume 350 operating days in a calendar year).

clarifying_info.q: What is the average stay and rate?
clarifying_info.a: Average duration of stay is 4 nights; average hotel check is $2,000.
Mandarin Oriental and Four Seasons have already entered (250 rooms each). Other hotel chains considering entry include Starwood, Peninsula, and Imperial Hotels.

clarifying_info.q: What are the barriers to entry?
clarifying_info.a: Government regulations, high capital requirements, and unavailable beachfront property.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's ROI target?
clarifying_info.a: At a 10% ROI, the company's target is to recover its investment within one year.

clarifying_info.q: What are the operating assumptions for the ROI analysis?
clarifying_info.a: Average occupancy is 50%; 350 operating days per year; operating expenses are 100% variable.

exhibits.title: Three Available Lots - Key Financials
exhibits.shows: A table comparing three shortlisted property options across five dimensions: land cost, cost per room, operating cost per room per night, room capacity, and price per night.

framework: Core Competencies - assess whether client has relevant skills for hotel development and operations
Market Attractiveness - size the market, apply Five Forces (competition, supplier power, buyer power, substitutes, barriers to entry)
ROI Analysis - calculate and compare return on investment across the three shortlisted lots
Project Feasibility / Success Factors - identify practical concerns (financing, operating model, partnerships, government permits)
Go / No-Go Recommendation - synthesize findings into a supported decision

questions.prompt: What is the total market size in tourist nights per year, and what is the implied average nightly rate?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply tourists by average stay to get total tourist nights, then divide by operating days to get nightly demand. Separately derive average nightly rate by dividing total check by average stay.

math.setup: Total tourist nights = 875,000 tourists x 4 nights = 3,500,000 tourist nights/year. Nightly demand = 3,500,000 / 350 days = 10,000 tourists/night. Average nightly rate = $2,000 total check / 4 nights = $500/night.
math.answer: 10,000 tourists per night; $500 average nightly rate

questions.prompt: Calculate the ROI for each of the three shortlisted lots and identify which maximizes return.
questions.guidance: For each option: Operating Profit = (Price/Night - Operating Cost/Night) x Rooms x 350 days x 50% occupancy. Initial Investment = (Cost/Room x Rooms) + Land Cost. Net Profit = Operating Profit - Investment. ROI = Net Profit / Investment. Candidate should identify Fookwah Heights as the highest ROI option exceeding the 10% target.

math.setup: Operating Profit = (Price - OpCost) x Rooms x 350 x 0.50. Investment = (Cost/Room x Rooms) + Land Cost. ROI = (Operating Profit - Investment) / Investment.
steps: Lover's Lair: Op Profit = ($450-$250) x 500 x 350 x 0.50 = $17.5M; Investment = $30K x 500 + $2M = $17M; Net = $0.5M; ROI = 0.5/17 = 2.9%
Paradise Lost: Op Profit = ($400-$200) x 1,000 x 350 x 0.50 = $35M; Investment = $28K x 1,000 + $4M = $32M; Net = $3M; ROI = 3/32 = 9.4%
Fookwah Heights: Op Profit = ($350-$150) x 1,500 x 350 x 0.50 = $52.5M; Investment = $25K x 1,500 + $6M = $43.5M; Net = $9M; ROI = 9/43.5 = 20.7%
math.answer: Fookwah Heights has the highest ROI at 20.7%, exceeding the 10% target. Paradise Lost is at 9.4% (just below target). Lover's Lair is at 2.9% (well below target).

questions.prompt: If the market room price of $500/night is used instead of the option-specific prices, how does the ROI picture change?
questions.guidance: Candidate should redo the revenue line using $500/night for all three options while keeping the same operating costs, room counts, and investment figures. This tests adaptability and shows that pricing assumptions materially affect the decision.

math.setup: Use $500/night as price for all three options; keep same operating costs, room counts, and investment figures.
steps: Lover's Lair at $500: Op Profit = ($500-$250) x 500 x 350 x 0.50 = $21.875M; Investment = $17M; Net = $4.875M; ROI ~ 28.7%
Paradise Lost at $500: Op Profit = ($500-$200) x 1,000 x 350 x 0.50 = $52.5M; Investment = $32M; Net = $20.5M; ROI ~ 64.1%
Fookwah Heights at $500: Op Profit = ($500-$150) x 1,500 x 350 x 0.50 = $91.875M; Investment = $43.5M; Net = $48.375M; ROI ~ 111.2%
math.answer: At the market rate of $500/night, all three options far exceed the 10% ROI target; Fookwah Heights remains the top choice with the highest absolute return.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors should the client consider in determining the feasibility of entering this market?

categories.name: Competitive Strategy
ideas: Decide where to compete on the spectrum: low cost, high service, best-in-class, or package offerings
Assess what existing competitors (Mandarin Oriental, Four Seasons) are focusing on and whether the market will be flooded

categories.name: Operating Model
ideas: Determine whether the client will manage the hotel themselves or build it and find an operating partner such as Starwood or Hilton
Leveraging an established operator could fill the gap in hotel and service operations experience

categories.name: Core Competency Leverage
ideas: The client has strong construction capabilities and a track record at prime beach locations
The client lacks direct hotel industry and service operations experience - this gap must be addressed

categories.name: Financing
ideas: Explore government incentives: since the hotel will create jobs, the government may offer tax deductions or free services
Evaluate equity vs. debt mix given the large capital requirement

categories.name: Regulatory and Infrastructure
ideas: Obtain necessary government permits for construction
Confirm access to sewage, water, and other utilities
Understand any restrictions on beachfront property development

categories.name: Market Risk
ideas: Tourism demand depends on government advertising spend, travel agents, and the network effect of existing hotels
Client competes against all other paradise-type destinations globally (Disneyland, Vegas, Bermuda, etc.)
Increasing buyer power from travel agency consolidation and e-vendors could pressure nightly rates

recommendation: Go: recommend entering the market, selecting Fookwah Heights (1,500 rooms) as it delivers the highest ROI at 20.7% - the only option clearly exceeding the 10% target on option-specific pricing, and dramatically superior at the $500 market rate
The client has relevant construction and location-selection expertise, the market is large (10,000 tourists/night at $500/night), and regional interest is high following the new airport
risks: Client has no hotel operations or service management experience - requires an experienced operating partner or significant hiring
Market may become more competitive as Starwood, Peninsula, and Imperial Hotels are also evaluating entry
Elevated buyer power from consolidated travel agencies and online booking platforms could compress nightly rates below the modeled $350-$450
Large capital outlay ($43.5M for Fookwah Heights) increases exposure if occupancy falls below 50%
next_steps: Identify and negotiate with a hotel operating partner (e.g., Starwood, Hilton) to manage service operations
Secure government permits and confirm infrastructure access (water, sewage) for Fookwah Heights
Conduct demand sensitivity analysis - assess breakeven occupancy and rate scenarios
Explore government incentives (tax breaks, subsidies) given the job-creation impact of a 1,500-room hotel
